synthesis.building_stock: The Sunshine-area locksmith serving Sunshine West frames its keyless and smart digital entry work as fitting "both modern and older homes" (auslock.com.au Sunshine North/Sunshine West page), so installers here cannot assume a single door standard — and a real Sunshine West Airtasker job reads "remove smart lock and install new smart lock and knob and also fill hole with filler if necessary", evidencing existing bore holes and cut-outs that do not line up with a new smart lock's footprint; the suburb also carries commercial and industrial property alongside residential (sentrylocksmiths.com.au Sunshine West page), so entry doors are not all domestic.
synthesis.demographic_skew: The only occupancy signal in the returned records is Sentry Locksmiths' Sunshine West page addressing "the owners and lessees of commercial, industrial and residential property" — a mixed owner-occupier and lessee base rather than a purely owner-occupied one — and residents are visibly sourcing lock work through Airtasker's Sunshine West listings, where the pitch is "FREE quotes in minutes", indicating buyers who compare quotes before committing; no age, income or household-composition signal was returned.
common_concerns: Whether a new smart lock will actually cover the holes left by the old hardware, or leave gaps needing filling — the live Sunshine West Airtasker locksmith job is literally "remove smart lock and install new smart lock and knob and also fill hole with filler if necessary".

Whether a smart lock can be fitted to an older home and not just a new one — the competitor covering Sunshine North/Sunshine West specifically advertises fitting keyless and smart digital entry to "both modern and older homes throughout the Sunshine area", which is a distinction being sold because customers ask about it.
How a smart lock coexists with a security mesh/screen door on the same entry — the same Sunshine West Airtasker thread includes "I want to install a security mesh door" alongside the smart lock swap.
